  PROBLEM: The numbered-section header regex on line 1619 accepts optional trailing punctuation (`[.:]?\s*$`) but the numbered-section stop regex on line 1620 requires trailing punctuation (`[.:]\s*$`), so a numbered section without trailing punctuation is never closed.
  WHY: Items from later sections that contain backtick-wrapped paths are evaluated against the wrong scope; the same asymmetry exists in `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:222-224`.

- scripts/security_audit.sh:1514 (cross_file_guard_deletion_pattern, function-call alternation) | severity=low | confidence=3

  WHY: A deleted line such as `has_(user)` or `can_(user)` can incorrectly trigger the cross-file guard and demote an access-control finding from advisory back to blocking.
